To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

starch accessibility is a major factor in the glycaemic response of starchy cereal foods; that the starch accessibility is modulated by many factors including the physical form of cereal endosperm, its amylose content, the presence of β-glucan, the formation of starch-lipids complexes, and the processing conditions of the cereal food; and that whole grain foods are intrinsicaly low GI but may also be beneficial in preventing obesity and diabetes because of their phytochemical composition.

In summary, our research is concerned with
developing starchy cereal foods with a low glycaemic response and a high satiety effect.
the development and application of new processing technologies to produce low GI starchy cereal foods, and with understanding the underlying principles of the low GI effect.
the development of starchy cereal foods with low GI and hence low glycaemic load to reduce obesity and related metabolic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best approach for reducing hyperglycaemia is to eat wholegrain starchy cereal foods with low GI and high fibre.

the most promising approaches for reducing starch digestibility in starchy cereal food products are to use high amylose starch, heat-moisture processing, high levels of barley or oat β-glucan, or a combination of these.
there are a number of ways to reduce the glycaemic response of starchy cereal foods but there is no one single technology to achieve this.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of strategies, including the use of whole grain, low GI, high amylose and high β-glucan starches and heat moisture treatment of starch, is needed to develop low GI cereal foods with high consumer acceptability.
the best way to improve the health benefits of starchy cereal foods is to use a combination of strategies, including low GI, whole grain, low energy density, and high satiety.
there is considerable scope for modulating glycaemia through starchy cereal products, but that the most effective approach may be to combine several of the approaches mentioned above.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of low GI cereal foods is feasible and that these may play a role in preventing obesity, insulin resistance and type 2-diabetes.
the starch in starchy cereal products can be manipulated in many ways to produce foods with low GI.
starchy cereal foods are not all the same in terms of their glycaemic response.
